_: The authority for what the drain may do unattended. tick.py refuses to emit a brief that would violate this file. Operator decision 2026-09-11.
_repo: Passed to every `gh` call as --repo. It is a POLICY input, never an accident of the working directory: `gh issue list` with no --repo resolves the repo from cwd, so running the harness from another checkout returned rc=0 and a valid-looking list for a DIFFERENT repository - whose numbers are disjoint from this ledger's, which would have moved all 297 items out of the queue in one save.

scope.definition_of_done: every open issue reaches closed | parked | declined

wip._: A policy INPUT, not a constant. The host carries ~66 GB committed before any agent starts (vmmemWSL 48 GB + llama-server ~18 GB), which is why three things were memory-killed on 2026-09-11. Lower this before blaming a command.

_estate: Operator decision 2026-09-12: RESUME ON DEMAND, PER DEPLOY ITEM. The estate stays paused; resume only when a W1 item is ready for its deploy-run receipt, take the receipt, re-pause. Both verbs are permitted unattended because a resume the harness cannot pause again is worse than one it can. Before this they were absent, so action_is_permitted() failed closed on them and every deploy-path receipt was unreachable.

review._: Operator decision 2026-09-12, after W0 took EIGHT POSTED rounds with two reviewers (count them: gh pr view 4483 --json comments). That intensity was right for the merge gate ITSELF and is not the default for ordinary lanes. Read by tick.write_brief so every lane is told its own review requirement, and re-decided by merge_gate gate 3b on the REAL changed files.
review._escalate: MACHINE-READABLE ON PURPOSE. The first version of this key was four English sentences while a hardcoded ESCALATION_PATHS tuple did the work -- so the list could be emptied, inverted or deleted and every decision stayed identical. That is the marker_any_of defect this module found and fixed two rounds ago, reintroduced one release later. That constant is now DELETED: gates.escalation_paths(policy) and gates.escalation_streams(policy) READ these lists, and eight mutation arms that edit ONLY this file are killed by the suite -- which is what gives the authority a blast radius.
review._paths: The last five were missing and each decides something this list exists to protect. .gitignore is #4468's ENTIRE THESIS -- an entry in it is what hid the merge gate. CODEOWNERS decides who must review. Makefile is the `make validate` entry point and pyproject.toml is the ruff/mypy config every guard runs under. portal/ is the OTHER web front-end, and ux-baseline.md scopes 'every CSA Loom front-end surface', not only apps/fiab-console.
review._streams: W6-ci is here because the policy's own sentence says 'or any guard' and W6-ci IS the guard stream. It was covered only incidentally -- stream_for assigns W6-ci BECAUSE the item carries lane:ci, which maps to scripts/ci, which escalates by path. But `stream` is pinned from the inventory snapshot while `lane` is refreshed from live labels every tick, so a relabel decouples them: measured, W6-ci with lane:dataplane got ONE reviewer. W4/W8/W9 are deliberately absent.
review._stream_unknown: FAILS CLOSED, and it is the merge-gate half of escalate_when_footprint_unknown. At BRIEF time the stream is a fact and the paths are a guess; at MERGE time the paths are a fact and the stream has to be resolved from the ledger via the issues the PR references. All three ways that fails - the PR references no issue, there is no ledger, or the issue is not in it - mean the harness cannot place the work, so it escalates rather than falling through to the default. Measured 2026-09-12: with only the path set passed, a csa_platform/security/auth.py diff on a W2-security item and an azure-functions/ diff on a W1-deploy item BOTH returned GO on one approval - and W1-deploy is the stream R1 says preempts everything. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, recorded rather than discovered later: the one-reviewer path needs a DECLARED close (Closes #N + --allow-close N) of an item the harness has IN FLIGHT - a MENTION only escalates, because a stale copy-pasted number must never buy a weaker gate - and --allow-close is itself refused until the item holds its receipt, which 0 of 299 do today. So the MERGE-GATE operating point is 100% two-reviewer (python tools/drain/operating_point.py --merge-gate). That is a DIFFERENT MEASUREMENT POINT from the 93% in _operating_point below, which is taken at BRIEF time from a lane before the diff exists and whose largest driver - footprint not known - cannot exist at merge time. They are not comparable and neither is 'up from' the other. It does NOT relax on its own: an item earns a receipt only through record_receipt(), which is now called in production by tick.py --record-receipt (it VERIFIES the evidence before writing, but does not verify the evidence is ABOUT the item - that binding is #4489). RE-MEASURE with tools/drain/operating_point.py --merge-gate once receipts exist; if it has not moved, bring the number back to the operator, because WIP is capped at 4 lanes and the ceiling is review capacity.
review._unknown: FAILS CLOSED. The escalation decision is taken from a LANE at brief time, before the diff exists, so the footprint is a guess. An unmapped lane, an item with no lane at all (119 of 299 live, including every W0-harness item), or a lane whose mapping is missing must escalate rather than fall through to the default. Every sibling control in this file fails closed; this one fell open.
review._operating_point: MEASURED 2026-09-12 over the live 299: 279 escalate (93%), 20 do not. THE 100 BELOW IS NOT THE UNLANED TOTAL - 119 items carry no lane, and 100 is what REMAINS attributed to 'footprint not known' after the stream trigger has already taken the other 19. Three numbers float around this package for the same idea (118 of 297 at open, 119 of 299 now, 100 attributed) and each is over a different population; say which one every time. Drivers: 100 'footprint not known' (91 of them W9-rest), then W5-console 84, W1-deploy 26, W6-ci 22, W2-security 20, W7-bicep 18, W0-harness 4, plus 3 console-path and 2 bicep-path (those last two are items whose STREAM does not escalate but whose lane path does -- the stream drivers alone sum to 274, not 279, and this is the file a reader checks arithmetic in). The operator was shown this and chose to LEAVE IT: most of the 93% is W9-rest, which is the TRIAGE stream and not schedulable until laned and sized anyway, so the steady-state figure is ~170 once triage runs. RE-MEASURE AFTER TRIAGE (python tools/drain/operating_point.py - TRACKED; it used to say temp/w0/, which is gitignored and therefore unrunnable on a fresh clone) rather than tuning the list on a pre-triage snapshot -- and if it is still near 93% with W9 laned, that is the number to bring back, because WIP is capped at 4 lanes and the ceiling is review capacity.
review.writer_is_never_the_reviewer: enforced by TOOL ACCESS, not by instruction: the reviewer agent is read-only

stop_and_ask._: Hard refusals. tick.py will not emit a brief containing these, and a lane that reports one must park the item.
stop_and_ask.publish_security_advisory: outward-facing and irreversible; operator decides once the fix is DEPLOYED
stop_and_ask.move_live_acr_tags: a branch dispatch of build-fiab-images-acr-tasks hard-codes --image <name>:latest and moves :latest AND :v0.1 for all 13 images in the live Commercial ACR
stop_and_ask.delete_data_or_schema: not reversible, and the blast radius is unknowable from inside a lane - a dropped container or column takes every downstream consumer with it
stop_and_ask.force_push_shared_branch: a stale worktree makes --force-with-lease unsafe; sweep first
stop_and_ask.weaken_or_baseline_a_guard: making something green by widening its allowlist is the defect, not the fix
stop_and_ask.add_trivyignore_entry: the baseline is deliberately EMPTY; fix the image
stop_and_ask.use_skip_valve: LOOM_BUILD_SKIP_SUPPLY_CHAIN / skip_uat / skip_signature_verify ship unverified or unsigned artifacts

receipt_producers._: WHICH WORKFLOW may be accepted as evidence for a run-backed receipt kind, read by `tick.record_receipt_from_evidence`. Fails CLOSED: a kind absent from this map cannot be auto-recorded at all, so widening the write path is a deliberate edit to this file and not an emergent behaviour. `operator` is deliberately ABSENT and must stay absent - a human-only receipt a program can record is not human-only. `ci-green` is absent for a different reason: it is not run-backed, it is re-MEASURED by gates.ci_green_receipt at record time. Only workflows a receipt has actually been taken from are listed; add one by taking a receipt from it first, never by predicting that it would work.

receipt_required_steps._: STEPS that must themselves have concluded success, over and above the run. ALL of them, and a kind with an empty list is refused rather than waved through. `receipts.g1_assertion_rule` requires the receipt to key on something ONLY a success path can produce, and a green RUN does not satisfy that for ANY of these kinds - which is the whole finding: the first version of this map wired the check to `g1-browser` alone and left `deploy-run` and `estate` run-level, closing the defect at its label instead of at its site. MEASURED: 2 of the last 25 successful `loom-roll-and-validate` runs carry `Roll image + validate live URL` = skipped, steps=0 (34575500655, 34573457723), and `cloud-parity.md` names that exact shape - 'a green run whose deploy job was skipped at 0 steps is not a receipt'. A skipped JOB reports no steps at all, so requiring a step INSIDE it catches the skipped-job case and the skipped-step case with one mechanism. Every step name here was read off a real green run, never guessed.
deploy-run: Roll Container App to new image
estate: Start (or adopt) a synthetic-monitor execution + poll to completion

receipts._: Which receipt closes which class of issue. deploy-integrity.md R2: merged is never done.
receipts.g1_assertion_rule: must key on something ONLY a success path can produce, and the receipt must NAME why it is unreachable from an error path. An assertion satisfied by 'Error: HTTP 500' is not a receipt.

ci_green_rule._: #4487. The OLD definition - 'every required context green AT THE MERGED SHA' - names a measurement this CI topology cannot produce, and that was found by trying to take the receipt for the first time. At a02cd41e6d42 (the merge of #4483): 15 required, 10 green, 5 absent, 0 red. Four of the five are published by validate.yml, whose push: trigger is path-filtered to bicep/deploy/workflow paths that merge did not touch; the fifth is commit-message-parses.yml publishing the PUSH spelling of a conditionally-named job. A definition the topology cannot satisfy leaves two outcomes - every guard/test-only issue is unclosable, or somebody quietly accepts 10-of-15 as green and the receipt stops meaning what it says.
ci_green_rule.definition: every required context that CAN run at the merged sha is green; every one that CANNOT is NAMED, with the reason it could not and its result on the PR head over an IDENTICAL TREE
ci_green_rule.absence_is_excused_only_when: the producing workflow - traced by workflow IDENTITY from the PR head, never by an alias table - either RAN at the merged sha and concluded SUCCESS under a different job name (the per-event rename case), or was NEVER CREATED there because its own on.push trigger, read AT that sha, could not have admitted the commit (the path-filter case)
ci_green_rule.fails_closed_on: an untraceable producer, an unreadable on.push trigger, a workflow that SHOULD have run and did not, a merged sha carrying zero check-runs at all, an empty required set, and a deferral to a PR head whose tree differs from the merged tree
ci_green_rule.not_proven_by_this_receipt: that any required context measured a non-empty POPULATION. statusCheckRollup publishes none, so green-over-zero-items (the #4451 shape) stays invisible here and remains an owed capability, not a claim.
ci_green_rule._substantive_steps: WHICH step a context must have EXECUTED, not how many. Measured 2026-09-13 over 24 green-at-merge contexts on PRs 4483 and 4488: a proportion cannot decide this. `vitest (node 20)` skipped `Run vitest (with istanbul coverage floor)` - the step that IS the check - at 38% skipped, while `Python Tests (3.10)` skipped only its trailing `Coverage summary` at 9%. Any threshold accepting the second accepts the first. Nor can it be inferred from names: `_is_bookkeeping_step` already misclassifies six real step names (`Post HIGH findings to PR`) in the EXCUSING direction. So it is DECLARED, per context, from evidence. A context ABSENT from this map FAILS CLOSED - add it with the step read off a real green run, never guessed. `ALL` means every work step must have run, for contexts whose work is distributed across many steps rather than concentrated in one.
ci_green_rule._alternatives: #4487 round 5, and it is the defect that mattered most: a job may have MORE THAN ONE work-gating output, and a row naming only the first makes the receipt SAY SOMETHING FALSE. `vitest (node 20)` runs `Run vitest (infra-reading suites only)` when console is untouched but `infra` changed - and `infra` is derived by scripts/ci/derive-infra-reading-suites.mjs from an ERE containing `tools/` and `PRPs/`, which is the exact footprint of a drain PR. MEASURED by an independent reviewer on the two merged shas this PR presents as its receipt (runs 34707045178 and 34665183833): the coverage-floor suite was skipped and the infra suite SUCCEEDED, while the receipt printed 'there was nothing for it to do'. It did work. Same shape for `next build (node 20)`'s `portal` output, which per that workflow's #4187 comment is the portal's only blocking check. So a declared ALTERNATIVE that RAN is the context doing its work, named in the evidence. ROUND 6 - WHERE THAT ACCEPTANCE IS MADE IS THE WHOLE CONTROL. It was made inside `context_did_its_work`, which receives no changed_files, so it returned a pass BEFORE the scope corroboration ran - and `_merged_files_outside_scope` is the only place a detector's output is checked against the merged commit's own file list. Both reviewers reproduced the consequence on different rows: with a console file in the merge and the detector wrongly reporting console=false, round 4 REFUSED ('a change detector that missed a change') and round 5 ACCEPTED as green-at-merge, naming the alternative. A required context certified green over a console that was never built or tested - the #3783 shape this file says must never be laundered, laundered by the fix for something else. So `alternative_accounted_for` asks BOTH questions: an alternative stands in for a skipped primary only when the merged files are outside every declared scope. It must also have concluded SUCCESS (not merely 'not skipped', which counts `failure` and `cancelled`), and it must NOT be the row's `gate_step` - the detector always runs, so declaring it would make the substantive-step rule vacuous for that context with a one-line edit here.
ci_green_rule._scope_paths: #4487 round 4. The substantive-step rule made `ci-green` UNOBTAINABLE FOR THE EXACT CLASS IT CLOSES: a guard/test-only PR by construction does not touch apps/fiab-console, so `next build (node 20)` and `vitest (node 20)` correctly skip their work behind an in-job change detector and conclude SUCCESS - and both drain merges in the window, #4483 and #4488, returned NOT GREEN for exactly those two. 0 for 2 on the population the receipt serves, which is #4487's own thesis one branch along. The receipt already excuses a PATH-FILTERED workflow by applying its declared filter to the merged commit's changed files; this is the SAME measurement for a filter that lives in a shell step instead of in on.push.paths, and the difference between those two is where GitHub lets you write a filter, not how much the merge was checked. `paths` are GitHub filter-pattern globs, read off the producing workflow's own change detector; __tests__/test_ci_green_declared.py fails if they drift from it. A context with no row here CANNOT reach the excuse at all, and a row whose scope MATCHES a merged file is a FAILURE, not an excuse - that is a detector that missed a change (#3783), which is the defect this must never launder. ROUND 6: THE UNIT IS THE OUTPUT, NOT THE CONTEXT. A row used to carry one `paths` list against a `gate_step` that emits SEVERAL outputs, and so corroborated only the first. `next build (node 20)` declared `console` while the same detector also emits `portal` (^portal/react-webapp/) - and that job is, per the workflow's own #4187 comment, the portal's ONLY blocking check, so a portal-only merge whose portal grep did not fire was excused with 'there was nothing for it to do' by the one required context that would have caught it. `vitest (node 20)` declared `console` while also emitting `infra`, whose scope is an ERE COMPUTED by scripts/ci/derive-infra-reading-suites.mjs and named in no row at all. Both were found by an independent reviewer. So `outputs` enumerates EVERY output that gates work, each with its own scope, and the excuse is granted only when every one of them provably excludes every merged file. An output that cannot be evaluated REFUSES. ROUND 8 - AND THIS SENTENCE USED TO END HERE, CLAIMING 'an under-declared row is now a refusal, not a silent pass'. It was false, and BOTH independent reviewers proved it independently: the refusal existed for an output PRESENT-BUT-UNEVALUABLE and never for an ABSENT one, because nothing compared this list against what the detector actually emits. Deleting the four-line `portal` block below left `391 passed` untouched and flipped a portal-only merge from refused to excused - round 6's blocker verbatim. What makes the sentence true now is an INSTRUMENT, not this note: `test_the_declared_scope_matches_the_workflows_own_change_detector` walks WORKFLOW -> DECLARED as well as declared -> workflow, asserting every `steps.<detector-id>.outputs.<X>` the job gates work on appears here; and arms R17/R18 in `mutate_gates.py` delete an output and must be KILLED, which is why the mutation sandbox now carries the workflow files this row names. A claim in this file that no arm can kill is prose.
ci_green_rule._job: The YAML job KEY, not the display name. Round 5: the drift guard matched on the context's display name and so read the WRONG job — both console rows resolved to the `build` job's detector and `vitest`'s, 250 lines down with a different second output, was never read. A display name is also not always present in the file: `Python Tests (3.10)` is a MATRIX job whose `name:` is `Python Tests (${{ matrix.python-version }})`, so the literal context name appears nowhere. The job key is exact, stable across a rename, and the thing a reader can find. ROUND 8 DISCLOSURE: `workflow` and `job` are read by the DRIFT TEST and by the mutation sandbox's workflow copy — no decision function resolves a row through them, so pointing either at something that does not exist changes no verdict and only the test notices. They are the guard's addressing, not the receipt's; do not read them as though `gates.py` consulted them.

scope_paths._python_tests: Same family, different shape, and it is the reason a `paths` may be the STRING "on.push.paths". test.yml's `Detect Python-relevant changes` does not carry its own path list: it delegates to scripts/ci/python_trigger_scope.py, which parses on.push.paths OUT OF test.yml - and that file's own comment says 'ONE list ... READ OUT OF THIS FILE - not a second copy of it that has to be kept in agreement by review'. Copying those 15 globs here would create precisely that second copy. So the row points at the trigger the receipt ALREADY parses, which is drift-free by construction. This job has ONE work-gating output, so its `outputs` list has one entry - the list is not padding, it is the shape that made the two-output rows above expressible. Measured on PR #4401 (console-only): test.yml is path-filtered out at the merged sha AND its PR-head job skipped `Run pytest with coverage` behind the same list, so all three legs returned FAIL under round 4's first draft - the console blocker one family over.

merge_gate._: Each key names a gate and maps to the function that IMPLEMENTS it. gates.MERGE_GATE_IMPLEMENTED_BY holds that mapping and tools/drain/__tests__/test_policy.py fails when a key here has no implementation, or an implementation no key. These were 10 keys READ BY NOTHING while both module docstrings described 'five policy keys read by nothing' as a repaired past defect - an unconsulted policy key is prose, not a control, including when the prose is about unconsulted policy keys.
merge_gate._removed_require_hollow_check_clean: DROPPED 2026-09-11. It asserted a capability the API cannot support: statusCheckRollup publishes no per-check population, so a check that concluded SUCCESS over ZERO items is invisible to this gate. What IS detectable - a required context that concluded SKIPPED - is now require_no_skipped_required_context. Detecting green-over-nothing is an owed capability, not a claim.
merge_gate._removed_clause5: DROPPED 2026-09-11. clause5_carries_artifact_only / clause5_refuses_source_change described carrying a void APPROVE across an artifact-only re-derive. Nothing implements it, and a verdict is pinned to the head it measured; re-review after a push instead.

verdict_parsing._: merge-gate reads ISSUE COMMENTS, not review events. A verdict registers only if all three hold. Every key here is READ by gates.parse_verdicts - tools/drain/__tests__/test_policy.py fails if one stops being consulted.
verdict_parsing.note: A verdict is announced by a LINE that BEGINS with a marker, inside the window, not quoted. Within that line the tokens are read in the order listed, so a hedged header resolves to the block. Prose elsewhere in the comment is NOT a verdict: scanning the whole body let a quoted header from a previous round decide the gate, and let a sentence ABOUT an approval register as one. A token in the window with no announcing line is reported as a near-miss and blocks when the token blocks - 'CHANGES REQUIRED' was silently discarded and cost two rounds on 2026-09-11.

ordering._: Execution order of the workstreams. A later stream may depend on an earlier one, never the reverse.
ordering.W9_reason: 118 issues carry no lane and 153 carry no size; neither can be safely scheduled, so triage gates the parallelism for every other stream

stop_conditions._: Conditions under which the harness halts the whole run rather than continuing.
stop_conditions.deploy_path_red: deploy-integrity R1 - a broken deploy path preempts all feature work; fix it before selecting anything else
stop_conditions.estate_behind_and_not_recovering: R3 - drift is a defect with an owner, not a background condition
stop_conditions.gate_tooling_untracked: a gate nobody can read cannot be trusted to merge; W0 must land first
